final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim using the same record. That reframing is analytically cleaner, but it does not cure the missing policy predicate. A caveated position can support `compliant_with_caveats` only when the caveat is a disclosure, monitoring, or limitation statement that is itself already authorized by the governing policy record. Here, the unresolved issue is not merely a narrative caveat; it is whether a material limitation for a named launch use case has been resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The admissible evidence shows materiality, an open legal review, and no evidence of disclosure text or approved risk acceptance. On that record, `certify_model` remains unsupported as compliant, even if overall launch readiness is otherwise supported.
remaining_concerns: The multilingual customer-support segment misses target by 1.1 percentage points and is named in two regional support commitments, which supports materiality under the stated policy.
The release policy requires a material limitation for a named launch use case to be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of final legal resolution, actual disclosure text, or approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not satisfy the specific disclosure or risk-acceptance predicate.
The product characterization of the segment as non-core and low-volume does not overcome materiality where named commitments exist and legal review remains open.
